clue.text: Arena made from soft metal? Thanks for nothing

indicators.note: 'X for nothing' means X is put in the place where nothing stood, swapping one letter out

parts.note: sodium is a metal soft enough to cut with a knife
ta is informal British for thanks
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sports venue built out of some soft metal, with a grudging thank-you for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In SODIUM the O (nothing) is replaced by TA (thanks), giving STADIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is a large sports ground with tiered seating, the modern form of an arena.

clue.text: Assuming food and drink is outside

indicators.note: one piece sits outside, around the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
tuck is British schoolchildren's slang for food and snacks

explanation.surface: Someone presumes that food and drink will be served outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: SUP is outside TUCK: S(TUCK)UP. 'Assuming' here means presumptuous, not supposing.
explanation.definitionFit: An assuming person is arrogant and presumptuous, the same as a snobbish, superior, haughty one.

clue.text: Removing clothes in celebration shows skill

indicators.note: taking off the clothes strips away the outside layer, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: Stripping off at a party demonstrates a certain talent.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY without its outer letters leaves ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean a craft or knack acquired by practice, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Associate of two Milan teams heading to training

indicators.note: of joins the pieces in sequence

parts.note: Inter and AC are Milan's two big football clubs

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A colleague of both Milan football clubs is on his way to a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate is to mix or have dealings with others, which is what interacting means.

clue.text: Submissive male? I'm frightened

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
eek is a squeal of fright

explanation.surface: A timid man admits he is scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek describes someone quiet, gentle and easily imposed on, so readily giving in to others.

clue.text: Low-key lecturer dismissed by time theme can be discerned

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: low-key means understated
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
by as in three by four, the multiplication sign
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A quiet lecturer is sacked after some time, and a theme starts to emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is not a link word here: it is the multiplication sign, as in three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtext is the underlying message of a work, a theme that can be discerned beneath what is actually said.

clue.text: Piece of information affected queues still

parts.note: a stat is a single statistic

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: News of a disruption leaves the queues standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb about the queues; it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque means like a statue: tall, dignified and motionless, so still as stone.

clue.text: Roll joint as exotic break with lady's ending

indicators.note: with puts the next piece alongside
something exotic is foreign and strange, so these letters are made unfamiliar

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone rolls a joint as an unusual break with a female friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll joint' reads as cannabis, but it is a joint (place) for rolls, bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint is slang for an establishment, and a bakery is the shop where bread rolls are made and sold.

clue.text: Time to get outspoken Reading Tories' leader evicted — a complete removal

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: someone evicted is thrown out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a reading spoken aloud for others to write down

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A Tory leader in the town of Reading is evicted by outspoken voters, removed completely.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is capitalised to look like the Berkshire town. DICTATION loses its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: Eradication is wiping something out entirely, root and branch, so it is total removal.

clue.text: Mostly split, and split again in deluge

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: split as a past participle means ripped
rent is another word for torn apart

explanation.surface: Something nearly torn, and then torn again, in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing stream of water, so it is a flood or deluge.

clue.text: Acceptable? It's for victim to decide

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of a satisfactory standard
second meaning, read literally: the choice rests with the mark, a con artist's target

explanation.walkthrough: A mark is the victim of a swindle, so something left to the victim's decision is literally up to the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meeting the required standard, which is satisfactory or good enough to pass.

clue.text: Stubbly, perhaps: shaved for broadcast

indicators.note: shaving takes off what is at the edges, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a stubbly chin is one example of a hairy one, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: An unshaven man tidies up his stubble before going on television.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIRY with both ends shaved off leaves AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme is to transmit it, so the verb is a straightforward synonym for broadcasting something.

clue.text: King fires cooks making drinks

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it over into a different form, and to cook the books is to rig them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch dismisses his chefs and so has to make the drinks himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King fires cooks' reads as a sacking; 'fires' is the fodder and 'cooks' the verb working on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kefir is a fermented milk drink from the Caucasus, so the plural names servings of that beverage.

clue.text: Office and flats converted for the birds and the bees

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken as written, joined by and

explanation.surface: Office blocks and flats are being converted into homes for birds and bees.
explanation.definitionFit: The birds and the bees is a coy idiom for the basic information about sex and reproduction told to children.

clue.text: 25% of tequila drunk around 3rd of April

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters wrap themselves about another piece
someone drunk staggers about unsteadily, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the third letter of the following word is the one kept

parts.note: its third letter

explanation.surface: A quarter of the tequila is downed some time around early April.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a quartile marks off one quarter of a ranked data set, which is twenty-five per cent of it.

clue.text: Make harmless cadet a vet, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so these letters are dressed up anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker suggests a military cadet would make a veterinary surgeon who could defuse things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I think'; fancy is the anagram signal and I is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To deactivate a bomb or device is to stop it working, rendering it safe and no longer dangerous.

clue.text: Hummus's key ingredient, according to Spooner, is fruit of mallow

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words

parts.note: hummus is made mainly from chickpeas; swap the opening sounds of the two halves

explanation.surface: A cook claims the main ingredient of hummus is really a little mallow seed.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of CHICK and PEAS gives PICK CHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: The round flat seed head of the common mallow is called a cheese, and pick-cheese is a country name for it.

clue.text: Is unable to tip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the contraction of cannot
second meaning: to tilt or slope

explanation.walkthrough: Without its apostrophe the contraction is also a word for leaning over at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Can't is the short form of cannot, and cant as a verb means to slope or tilt sideways.

clue.text: Small window in stairs blocked by cane, essentially

indicators.note: a passage blocked by something has that thing lodged inside it

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its middle letters are kept

parts.note: its middle letters

explanation.surface: A little window over the staircase is jammed shut by a walking cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a small semicircular window above a door, often with radiating glazing bars like a fan.

clue.text: Racing driver who finished second several times

definitions.text: Racing driver who finished second several times

parts.note: surface reading: any motorist who never quite won
setter's reading: the British driver famously runner-up in the Formula One championship four years running

explanation.walkthrough: Stirling Moss was a celebrated British driver of the 1950s, often called the greatest never to win the world title.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirling Moss came second in the drivers' world championship four consecutive seasons, from 1955 to 1958.

clue.text: Heartlessly, not supporting the papers etc. giving the third degree

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece comes after
without a heart means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
newspapers, television and so on make up the media

explanation.surface: Cruelly refusing to back the press, someone faces a harsh grilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The third degree' suggests interrogation; in music it is the third note of a scale. NOT loses its middle O.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory the mediant is the third note of a diatonic scale, midway between tonic and dominant.

clue.text: Allegation from conservative Americans in lawsuit

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: an action is a case brought in court
C is the abbreviation for conservative
the USA stands for the American people collectively

explanation.surface: Right-wing Americans file a lawsuit making an allegation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation is a charge of wrongdoing, which is what an allegation claims against someone.

clue.text: Duke is grabbed by testicles; they are barely visible

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside another's grip

parts.note: nuts is slang for testicles
D is the abbreviation for duke
taken as written; it does double duty with the indicator

explanation.surface: A nobleman suffers a painful grab below the belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely visible' sounds like faint, but it means visible in the bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists go about naked, so they are seen bare, a pun on hardly visible.

clue.text: Dad's favourite child, affectionately

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A father fondly singles out his favourite child.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is a British term of endearment for a small child, like sweetheart or darling.

clue.text: Cover of Vogue inverted flower

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, which in a down-reading sense flips the letter order

parts.note: a lid covers a container
taken as written
a vogue is a passing fashion

explanation.surface: A magazine cover has been printed upside down with a flower on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover of Vogue' suggests a magazine front page, but it is three separate pieces read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A daffodil is a yellow spring flower with a trumpet-shaped centre.

clue.text: Half-heartedly had rings left to be copied

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece goes around the other
only half of the word's doubled central part is kept, so one of its middle letters goes

parts.note: to be had is to be tricked
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone who half-heartedly wore rings left them to be copied by a jeweller.
explanation.walkthrough: CONNED loses one of its middle Ns to give CONED, which then rings L: C(L)ONED.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone is to produce an exact genetic or digital duplicate, so it means reproduced or copied.

clue.text: Stain book, on the whole

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
the lot means everything, the whole

explanation.surface: Someone stains a book, all over its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the whole' reads as 'generally'; it splits into on (above) and the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a spot or smudge of ink, a mark that spoils a page.

clue.text: I see one fish

parts.note: ah is what you say when you see, i.e. understand
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone peering into the water spots a single fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahi is the Hawaiian name for yellowfin or bigeye tuna, a large ocean fish often served raw.

clue.text: Heads over ahead of schedule; good to make heavenly entrance

indicators.note: over means covering or spanning, so the first piece is laid around the others

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
arriving before the time set
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Heads covered and arriving early, the righteous make their way into heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: PATES goes over EARLY and G: P(EARLY G)ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearly gates are the traditional entrance to Heaven, guarded by Saint Peter, from the Book of Revelation.

clue.text: Regularly train to obtain bronze

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Train regularly to win a bronze medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze and tan are both words for the brown colour skin turns in the sun.

clue.text: Settler's unusual support structure

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pioneer builds an odd framework on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs and a crossbar used to hold up a table top or a bridge.

clue.text: Offensive publication despised in Liverpool sent back after a complaint

indicators.note: after places the turned-round word following the other pieces

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War
taken as written

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: The Sun newspaper has been boycotted in Liverpool since its Hillsborough coverage in 1989

explanation.surface: A notorious newspaper is returned to the sender after a reader's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive publication' reads as one phrase, but Offensive is TET on its own; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint is used for an illness or ailment, and tetanus is a bacterial disease causing muscle spasms.
